## 1 Configuration

Edit the variables in this chunk only — everything else runs automatically.

```{r config}
# ── File ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
file_path <- "../data/HOBO_AGATE_LOW_20260908.csv"   # path to your HOBO CSV export
tz        <- "America/Los_Angeles"    # logger timezone (PDT = America/Los_Angeles)

# ── Sample Point 1 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sp1_label <- "Sample Point 1"
sp1_start <- as.POSIXct("2026-07-13 10:07:03", tz = tz)   # first data point
sp1_end   <- as.POSIXct("2026-08-11 10:07:03", tz = tz)   # ~10 am Aug 9

# ── Sample Point 2 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sp2_label <- "Sample Point 2"
sp2_start <- as.POSIXct("2026-07-13 10:07:03", tz = tz)   # first data point
sp2_end   <- as.POSIXct("2026-09-08 00:00:00", tz = tz)   # through Sep 6 (all data)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2 Load packages

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)   # data wrangling + ggplot2
library(lubridate)   # datetime helpers
library(scales)      # axis formatting
library(knitr)       # kable tables
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3 Import & filter data

```{r import}
# Read raw CSV and standardise column names
raw <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
colnames(raw) <- c("row_id", "datetime_raw", "temp_c")

# Parse datetimes; keep all rows for reference
df_all <- raw %>%
  mutate(
    datetime = mdy_hms(datetime_raw, tz = tz),
    date     = as_date(datetime)
  ) %>%
  select(row_id, datetime, date, temp_c) %>%
  arrange(datetime)

# Filter to each sample period
sp1 <- df_all %>% filter(datetime >= sp1_start & datetime <= sp1_end)
sp2 <- df_all %>% filter(datetime >= sp2_start & datetime <= sp2_end)

cat(sp1_label, "— records:", nrow(sp1),
    " |", format(min(sp1$datetime)), "→", format(max(sp1$datetime)), "\n")
cat(sp2_label, "— records:", nrow(sp2),
    " |", format(min(sp2$datetime)), "→", format(max(sp2$datetime)), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4 Summary statistics

```{r summary-functions}
# Statistical mode helper
stat_mode <- function(x) {
  x  <- x[!is.na(x)]
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

# Reusable summary function
make_summary <- function(dat, label) {
  dat %>%
    summarise(
      sample_point = label,
      start        = format(min(datetime)),
      end          = format(max(datetime)),
      n            = n(),
      mean_c       = round(mean(temp_c,   na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      median_c     = round(median(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      mode_c       = round(stat_mode(temp_c),            3),
      min_c        = round(min(temp_c,    na.rm = TRUE),  3),
      max_c        = round(max(temp_c,    na.rm = TRUE),  3),
      sd_c         = round(sd(temp_c,     na.rm = TRUE),  3),
      range_c      = round(max_c - min_c,                 3)
    )
}
```

### 4.1 Overall summary — both sample points

```{r summary-overall}
summary_combined <- bind_rows(
  make_summary(sp1, sp1_label),
  make_summary(sp2, sp2_label)
)

kable(
  summary_combined,
  col.names = c("Sample Point", "Start", "End", "N",
                "Mean (°C)", "Median (°C)", "Mode (°C)",
                "Min (°C)", "Max (°C)", "SD (°C)", "Range (°C)"),
  caption   = "Temperature summary by sample point"
)
```

### 4.2 Daily summaries

```{r daily-summaries}
make_daily <- function(dat) {
  dat %>%
    group_by(date) %>%
    summarise(
      n        = n(),
      mean_c   = round(mean(temp_c,   na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      median_c = round(median(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      min_c    = round(min(temp_c,    na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      max_c    = round(max(temp_c,    na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      sd_c     = round(sd(temp_c,     na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      .groups  = "drop"
    )
}

daily_sp1 <- make_daily(sp1)
daily_sp2 <- make_daily(sp2)
```

**`r sp1_label` — daily summary**

```{r daily-sp1}
kable(daily_sp1,
      col.names = c("Date", "N", "Mean (°C)", "Median (°C)",
                    "Min (°C)", "Max (°C)", "SD (°C)"),
      caption   = paste(sp1_label, "— daily temperature summary"))
```

**`r sp2_label` — daily summary**

```{r daily-sp2}
kable(daily_sp2,
      col.names = c("Date", "N", "Mean (°C)", "Median (°C)",
                    "Min (°C)", "Max (°C)", "SD (°C)"),
      caption   = paste(sp2_label, "— daily temperature summary"))
```

## 5 Plots

Helper objects used across all plots:

```{r plot-helpers}
# Combine both periods into a long data frame for overlay plots
df_long <- bind_rows(
  sp1 %>% mutate(sample_point = sp1_label),
  sp2 %>% mutate(sample_point = sp2_label)
)

sp_colours <- c("#2196F3", "#E53935")          # SP1 = blue, SP2 = red
names(sp_colours) <- c(sp1_label, sp2_label)
```

### 5.1 Time series — each sample point

```{r plot-timeseries-sp1, fig.cap="SP1 temperature time series."}
plot_ts <- function(dat, label, colour) {
  mn <- mean(dat$temp_c, na.rm = TRUE)
  ggplot(dat, aes(x = datetime, y = temp_c)) +
    geom_line(colour = colour, linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = mn, linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
    annotate("text",
             x = min(dat$datetime), y = mn + 0.25,
             label = paste0("Mean = ", round(mn, 2), " °C"),
             hjust = 0, size = 3.2, colour = "grey30") +
    scale_x_datetime(labels = date_format("%b %d"), breaks = "1 week") +
    labs(
      title    = paste(label, "— Temperature Over Time"),
      subtitle = paste(format(min(dat$datetime), "%Y-%m-%d"),
                       "to",
                       format(max(dat$datetime), "%Y-%m-%d")),
      x = NULL, y = "Temperature (°C)"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

plot_ts(sp1, sp1_label, sp_colours[sp1_label])
```

```{r plot-timeseries-sp2, fig.cap="SP2 temperature time series."}
plot_ts(sp2, sp2_label, sp_colours[sp2_label])
```

### 5.2 Overlay — both sample points on one axis

```{r plot-overlay, fig.cap="Both sample periods overlaid. SP1 ends at the dashed vertical line."}
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = datetime, y = temp_c, colour = sample_point)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(sp1_end),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = sp1_end, y = Inf, vjust = -0.4, hjust = 1.05,
           label = "SP1 end", size = 3, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sp_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_datetime(labels = date_format("%b %d"), breaks = "1 week") +
  labs(
    title    = "Temperature Agate Pass (-1' MLLW)",
    subtitle = "Dashed line marks the end of Sample Point 1",
    x = NULL, y = "Temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "none")
```

### 5.3 Daily min / mean / max ribbon — each sample point

```{r plot-ribbon, fig.cap="Daily mean (line) with min–max ribbon for each sample point.", fig.height=8}
plot_ribbon <- function(daily_dat, label, colour) {
  ggplot(daily_dat, aes(x = date)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = min_c, ymax = max_c),
                fill = colour, alpha = 0.25) +
    geom_line(aes(y = mean_c), colour = colour, linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(aes(y = mean_c), colour = colour, size = 1.5) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 week", date_labels = "%b %d") +
    labs(
      title    = paste(label, "— Daily Temperature"),
      subtitle = "Line = daily mean  |  Ribbon = daily min–max range",
      x = NULL, y = "Temperature (°C)"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

p_r1 <- plot_ribbon(daily_sp1, sp1_label, sp_colours[sp1_label])
p_r2 <- plot_ribbon(daily_sp2, sp2_label, sp_colours[sp2_label])

# Stack both plots (requires patchwork; falls back to separate plots if absent)
if (requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(patchwork)
  p_r1 / p_r2
} else {
  print(p_r1)
  print(p_r2)
}
```

### 5.4 Diel pattern — both sample points

```{r plot-diel, fig.cap="Mean temperature ± 1 SD by hour of day for each sample point."}
diel_long <- df_long %>%
  mutate(hour = hour(datetime)) %>%
  group_by(sample_point, hour) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_c = mean(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_c   = sd(temp_c,   na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(diel_long, aes(x = hour, y = mean_c,
                      colour = sample_point, fill = sample_point)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_c - sd_c, ymax = mean_c + sd_c),
              alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sp_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = sp_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3),
                     labels = function(h) sprintf("%02d:00", h)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Diel Temperature Pattern",
    subtitle = "Mean ± 1 SD by hour of day",
    x = "Hour of day", y = "Temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top")
```

### 5.5 Temperature distribution — both sample points

```{r plot-histogram, fig.cap="Temperature distribution for each sample point."}
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = temp_c, colour = sample_point, fill = sample_point)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(
    data = df_long %>%
      group_by(sample_point) %>%
      summarise(mean_c = mean(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    aes(xintercept = mean_c, colour = sample_point),
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sp_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = sp_colours, name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title    = "Temperature Distribution",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines = group means",
    x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top")
```
